points.description: States that height is the length of the longest path (the maximum number of edges/levels along a path) in the tree, i.e. the maximum over all paths, not just any path.
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if 'longest/maximum path' is stated but length is not made explicit, or length is given but 'longest' is imprecise

points.description: States that the path runs from the root down to a leaf (a node with no children), using the terms 'root' and 'leaf'.
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if only one endpoint (root or leaf) is named correctly

points.description: Correctly distinguishes height from depth: height is measured from the root to the deepest leaf for the whole tree, not the depth/level of a single arbitrary node, and not the number of nodes in the tree.

rubric.notes: Full marks need the precise statement: height = length of the longest path from the root to a leaf, using the terms 'longest', 'root' and 'leaf'. Part marks only where clearly more than half of a point is stated precisely. Vague answers (e.g. 'how tall the tree is', 'number of levels' without longest path, 'number of nodes') earn nothing, and a wrong statement (shortest path, or confusing with depth or size) loses that point.
